thread:
oncall-bot: PAGER — High 95th latency on /v1/generate in us-west-2 (SLO risk). Alert triggered at 1976543209. paging @oncall now :rotating_light:

maya: taking this. I see a spike in p95 at ~18:12 UTC, correlated with a big burst from a partner batch job.

samir: +1, I can look at infra side (GPU queue / pod restarts).

maya: quick mitigation plan: 1) scale up dedicated pool by +2 nodes, 2) enable aggressive KV prefix caching for common prompts, 3) fallback rule to lower-cost model variant for non-privileged routes. doing (1) now.

ops-bot: Scale request accepted. Added 2 nodes to pool-redwood-dedicated-usw2 (expected up in ~90s).

jonah: FYI I already saw a canary rolling at 18:05, might be related. @maya can you confirm if we rolled a new runtime kernel?

maya: checked — no kernel roll. Canary was a routing tweak (split 10/90) for model-quantization tests. I've paused routing to see if that helps.

carla: customer-impact check: Support funnel shows 12 errors in the last 20m, 3 timeouts reported from two customers in EU region (proxied through us-west). Might be transient but worth noting.

lee: logs show increased queue length on node gpu-12 and some 502s from envoy timeouts.

maya: scale is up. Initial tail latency improving but still noisy. I'm enabling prefix cache for top 50 prompts (experiment flagged).

emily: thanks — I'm opening a short incident thread in #incidents for external comms if needed.

----- 40 minutes later (mitigation complete) -----

maya: tl;dr: scaled pool +2 nodes, paused routing canary, enabled extra prefix caching, reduced per-request max tokens for experimental routes. p95 dropped from ~1.2s to ~410ms and error rate back to baseline. No further pages.

oncall-bot: Incident status: mitigated at 1976543600. Please do post-incident review and alert tuning if needed.

jonah: thanks. Postmortem / retro items: alert threshold tuning, reduce noise from canary metrics, dashboard improvements for quicker triage.

samir: agreed — current alert YML is firing on `api_request_latency_seconds{route=~"/v1/generate.*"}` p95 > 500ms for 2 consecutive 1m windows. That was noisy because of short lived partner burst. Suggest we change to p95 > 700ms for 5m for global, and create a separate canary alert for routing-induced anomalies (smaller scope).

carla: also recommend adding customer-impact panel to dashboard so SRE/support can quickly see which customers/routes saw errors (top 10 by error count).

maya: +1. I'm going to propose a new Grafana dashboard tailored to incident retrospectives. Key panels I want:
- Golden signals row: p50/p95/p99 latency, request rate, error rate, downstream saturation (GPU util), queue length
- Tail latency heatmap (1m buckets) for last 24h
- Per-route table: requests, errors, p95, recent deploys / routing variants (join to rollout tags)
- KV cache hit ratio timeseries
- Active canaries / routing splits (annotation layer)
- Customer-impact table (customer_id, route, errors, first_seen) with a link to runbook/incident ticket

jonah: love it. For queries, use existing metrics. Example heatmap query for latency: ```histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket{route=~"/v1/generate.*"}[5m])) by (le))```

samir: for GPU saturation: ```avg(avg_over_time(gpu_utilization_percent[5m])) by (instance)``` — but better to show node-level and cluster-level panels.

ash (ops-bot): Note: make sure dashboard has a short-lived panel for active autoscale events — we want to see scaling actions that map to performance change.

maya: action items I'm taking now:
1) Open PR for alert rule changes (p95 thresholds and for canary-scoped alert). -> PR #789 in infra-alerts repo.
2) Start a Grafana dashboard draft: https://grafana.company/d/incident-retrospective/ (working link; draft saved).
3) Add runbook links to dashboard panels.

carla: i'll add a small support-friendly panel that shows high-level customer impact summary (counts + affected customer names) so support can paste in comms.

lee: can we add a drilldown from p95 panel to a per-request trace sample? if we wire it to our tracing (tempo), that'll speed triage.

jonah: yes — add a link variable for trace query: `trace_id` from logs. Panel action: `Open traces for top-5 traces by duration`

emily: I'll schedule a 30m retro in #eng-sre for tomorrow to walk through the dashboard and finalize alert tuning. 

maya: I'll drop a small example JSON for a dashboard panel in the PR to speed reviews. Example panel snippet for per-route table:
```json
{
  "type": "table",
  "title": "Per-route errors & p95",
  "targets": [
    {"expr": "sum(rate(requests_error_total{route=~\"/v1/generate.*\"}[5m])) by (route)", "refId": "A"},
    {"expr": "histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket{route=~\"/v1/generate.*\"}[5m])) by (le,route)) by (route)", "refId": "B"}
  ]
}
```

samir: small note: include a panel showing `kv_cache_hit_ratio` as a single stat with sparkline, because we relied on cache in mitigation.

maya: assigned tasks: PR #789 (samir), dashboard draft (maya + jonah), support panel (carla), trace drilldown (lee), retro meeting (emily).

jonah: also tagging infra team to review autoscaler behavior during this spike — there was ~40s to provision nodes which is borderline for our SLOs.

carla: for alert noise, suggest adding a suppression window tied to large partner jobs (label `partner_job=true`) — if partner_job label present, route to a reduced-sensitivity alert.

maya: good idea. We'll add that to the PR as an annotation-based suppression.

----- End summary -----

maya: if everyone is happy i'll merge alert PR after reviews and push the dashboard to ops folder as draft. ping me if you want early access to the grafana draft. :white_check_mark:

jonah: thanks all, great teamwork. closing thread for now, will follow up in the retro tomorrow.

ops-bot: Note: This thread will be archived in 90 days.
